admin.alloc.backing.cashHint: Units were paid for into the fund's cash, and a redemption pays out of it at NAV.
admin.alloc.backing.confirmCash: Mark {service} as cash-backed. Redeem will pay holders out of the fund's cash at NAV — make sure that cash is actually there.
admin.alloc.backing.confirmInKind: Mark {service} as in-kind. Redeem will be refused, and holders exit by selling their units on the book.
admin.alloc.backing.inKindHint: Units stand for an asset the holders own off-platform. The fund holds no cash for them, so Redeem is refused and holders exit through the book.
admin.alloc.backing.title: Backing
admin.alloc.book.closedHint: Orders are refused; the book stays readable
admin.alloc.book.keepHint: Leave empty to keep the current value.
admin.alloc.book.note: The book is the secondary market in this product's units: holders trade with each other at the book's price, not at NAV. Opening it needs no valuation.
admin.alloc.book.openHint: Holders can place and fill orders
admin.alloc.book.problem.fee: Enter a percent between 0 and 100 with up to two decimals
admin.alloc.book.slippageHint: How far past the best level a market order may sweep.
admin.alloc.book.takerFeeHint: Charged to the side that crosses the spread, in USDT on the order value.
admin.alloc.book.title: Order book
admin.alloc.book.unbacked.ack: Allow trading of units not backed by fund cash
admin.alloc.book.unbacked.required: This product is held in kind: tick the acknowledgement before opening its book.
admin.alloc.book.unbacked.warning: Buyers pay cash for a claim on an asset held in kind and cannot redeem it — the book is their only exit
admin.alloc.emptyHint: Until one is, every subscription is refused.
admin.alloc.field.title: Title
admin.alloc.footnote: Registration lands in {state}, which takes no money — opening is a separate decision. Closing stops new subscriptions only: investors can always redeem out of a closed product, so winding one down never strands their units. The service id is permanent once registered. The unit cap bounds how many units may ever be issued — resize it on the Valuation screen, where the issued figure it is judged against is on the same page.
admin.alloc.grants.emptyHint: Every investor holds this product's default access until you raise one above it.
admin.alloc.hint.closed: Closed to new money; redemptions still settle
admin.alloc.hint.draft: Registered — accepts no money until opened
admin.alloc.holders.emptyHint: The split by holder appears once a subscription or an in-kind issuance mints the first unit.
admin.alloc.holders.title: Holders
admin.alloc.issue.costBasisHint: Optional — defaults to units × NAV at the current mark. Zero is allowed: a stake in an asset the holder already owned cost them no cash.
admin.alloc.issue.note: In kind: no cash moves. The units count against the cap like a subscription would, and the cost basis is what the holder is deemed to have paid.
admin.alloc.issue.problem.costBasis: Cost basis must be a decimal USDT amount
admin.alloc.issue.problem.units: Units must be a decimal number above zero
admin.alloc.issue.resultQueued: {units} units to {holder} queued — the relay posts the mint shortly, and the split below follows.
admin.alloc.issue.title: Issue units
admin.alloc.pinCap.alreadyPinned: The cap already equals the issued supply.
admin.alloc.pinCap.confirm: Cap {from} → {to}. No further units can be issued until the cap is raised again.
admin.alloc.pinCap.nothingIssued: Nothing has settled yet — a queued mint is not on the ledger until the relay posts it.
admin.alloc.pinCap.queued: {units} units are still queued in the relay — pin the cap once they have landed.
admin.alloc.placeholder.summary: One line for the catalog card
admin.alloc.registerHint: Registers in draft — open it when the product is ready to take money.
admin.alloc.retire.closeFirst: Close the product first — units are retired out of a wound-down product.
admin.alloc.retire.confirm: Retire {units} units from {holder} — the supply shrinks. No cash moves.
admin.alloc.retire.costBasisHint: Optional — the book value written off, defaults to units × NAV at the current mark.
admin.alloc.retire.forceConfirm: Forced: the product is not closed.
admin.alloc.retire.forceWarning: The product is still live — units will be burned out of it while it accepts money. The hub records the override.
admin.alloc.retire.investorHint: Up to what the investor holds — the hub refuses more, and says so.
admin.alloc.retire.resultQueued: {units} units from {holder} queued for retirement — the relay posts the burn shortly, and the split below follows.
admin.alloc.slugHint: Permanent — every fund RPC keys on it
admin.alloc.subtitle: The registry of investable products — a fund exists only once it is registered here
admin.fees.awaitingBody: The owners have each been emailed a link. Version {version} is scheduled only once more than half of them approve, and binds 24 hours after that while anyone holds units. The live tally is in the consilium.
admin.fees.awaitingTitle: Sent to the owners — nothing has changed yet
admin.fees.basisNote: Invested capital is the house default: it does not swell with a mark you posted, so what the manager earns stays independent of the input the manager supplies.
admin.fees.cancelWarning: Cancelling withdraws the change. The fund keeps its current terms, and the holders who were notified will not see the new ones.
admin.fees.cancelWarningAwaiting: Cancelling withdraws the change and takes its consilium down with it, voiding every approval collected so far. The owners who have already answered would each have to answer again.
admin.fees.collectedSub: Units the sweeper has clawed back from holders. No cash has moved yet.
admin.fees.crystallizationNote: A price, not a detail — crystallizing more often measurably raises what an investor pays over a fund's life, because each reset locks in gains a later loss can no longer claw back.
admin.fees.dateTime.placeholder: As soon as the notice allows
admin.fees.effectiveFromHint: Leave empty for the earliest allowed. While anyone holds units, a change binds no earlier than 24 hours after it is scheduled — counted from the owners' approval when they must give it. An earlier moment is lifted to that minimum, never refused.
admin.fees.effectiveFromLifted: Earlier than the notice allows: while anyone holds units, this binds no earlier than {floor}.
admin.fees.effectiveFromLiftedConsilium: Earlier than the notice allows: this binds no earlier than 24 hours after the owners approve.
admin.fees.err.notPercent: {field} must be a percentage — 2, or 2.5 / 2,5 for a half.
admin.fees.err.reasonRequired: A reason is required when the owners must approve.
admin.fees.err.reasonTooLong: The reason is too long: {used, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}} of at most {max}. Letters outside plain Latin count as more than one.
admin.fees.err.tooFarAhead: The moment can be at most {days} days ahead.
admin.fees.forbidden.body: Pricing a product changes what investors pay, so only an administrator or an owner can view and schedule fee terms. The rest of the console is yours as usual.
admin.fees.forbidden.title: Fee terms are set by administrators and owners
admin.fees.immediateBody: Nobody holds units in this product, so no notice was due: version {version} takes effect now and is applied within a minute. Until it is, it can still be cancelled below. The first investor to subscribe reads these terms.
admin.fees.immediateTitle: In force within a minute — nobody to notify
admin.fees.inForce: Version {version}, in force since {since}. Investors see these on the product page.
admin.fees.noChargesHint: The sweeper charges a holding once its accrual is old enough. Nothing here means nobody has been billed.
admin.fees.noFundsHint: A fee is a property of a product. Register an allocation first, then price it here.
admin.fees.noHistoryHint: Every version of this fund's terms will be listed here — what was scheduled, when it bound, and why.
admin.fees.notConfigured: This fund charges nothing today. Scheduling terms starts the clock on every holding in it from the moment they take effect.
admin.fees.nothingToSettle: Nothing to settle — no fee has been charged in this fund yet.
admin.fees.notices.acknowledgeWarning: The terms will bind over {n, plural, one {this holder} other {these # holders}} without their notice — tighter terms they were never told about. Your name, the moment, and exactly which holders it covers are recorded on the change and stay in its history.
admin.fees.notices.acknowledgeWarningExt: The terms will bind over {n, plural, one {this holder} other {these # holders}} without their notice — tighter terms they were never told about. Your name and the moment replace the earlier acknowledgement's on the change, which will then cover {total, plural, one {# holder} other {all # holders}}, and stay in its history.
admin.fees.notices.alreadyWaived: {by} already took responsibility on {at} for {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}} the mailer had given up on by then. It has given up on more since; this act adds them to that record.
admin.fees.notices.alreadyWaivedAnon: Responsibility was already taken on {at} for {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}} the mailer had given up on by then. It has given up on more since; this act adds them to that record.
admin.fees.notices.err.forbidden: Only the requester of this change or an owner can take responsibility for it.
admin.fees.notices.givenUpBody: The mailer has given up on {n, plural, one {this holder's notice} other {these # notices}}. A change that tightens the terms does not bind over a holder who was never told, so it is held up until somebody takes responsibility for them.
admin.fees.notices.givenUpTitle: {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}} could not be told
admin.fees.notices.moreQueued: {n, plural, one {# more notice is still being delivered and is not covered by this act.} other {# more notices are still being delivered and are not covered by this act.}}
admin.fees.notices.queued: {n, plural, one {# notice is} other {# notices are}} still being delivered. A change that tightens the terms waits for every holder to be told; there is nothing to do unless the mailer gives up on one.
admin.fees.pending.awaiting: Version {version} awaits the owners' approval. It binds 24 hours after they carry it, while anyone holds units.
admin.fees.pending.immediate: Version {version} takes effect now and is applied within a minute. Nobody holds units, so no notice was sent.
admin.fees.pending.scheduled: Version {version} takes effect on {at}. Holders have been notified.
admin.fees.pendingBlocks: One change at a time: cancel the pending one to schedule another.
admin.fees.reasonHint: Optional. Kept with this version in the history.
admin.fees.reasonRequiredHint: The owners read this in their approval mail, and it is part of what they sign.
admin.fees.requirement.admin: No vote needed: one administrator may make this change. Holders are mailed the notice when it is scheduled.
admin.fees.requirement.consilium: Needs the owners' approval: these terms tighten the current ones beyond the house 2 and 20, or lower the hurdle. You must be an owner to open the request.
admin.fees.scheduledBody: Version {version} takes effect on {at}. Every holder is being emailed the notice; until then the fund charges its current terms.
admin.fees.settleNote: Settling burns these units and moves their value from the fund's claim into fee revenue. It is refused — never queued — when the fund's claim cannot cover it on top of its queued redemptions: investors waiting to exit are paid before the manager is.
admin.fees.showcase.example: On a {amount} position: {management} a year, plus {performance} of any gain.
admin.fees.showcase.exampleHurdle: On a {amount} position: {management} a year, plus {performance} of any gain above a mark rising {hurdle} a year.
admin.fees.showcase.title: What gets saved
admin.fees.subtitle: What each fund charges its investors, and converting what it has already earned into cash.
admin.fees.title: Fee terms and collection
admin.fees.waiver.acknowledged: Notices waived by {by} on {at}, over {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}} who could not be told.
admin.fees.waiver.acknowledgedAnon: Notices waived on {at}, over {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}} who could not be told.
admin.fees.waiver.row: Notices waived by {by} · {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}}
admin.fees.waiver.rowAnon: Notices waived · {n, plural, one {# holder} other {# holders}}
admin.refusal.coolingBody: The list of owners changed within the last 48 hours. Payouts resume at {at}. The pause is deliberate: it keeps a change of ownership and a payout as two separate, visible events rather than one motion.
admin.refusal.coolingBodyNoTime: The list of owners changed within the last 48 hours, and payouts stay paused until that period lifts. The pause is deliberate: it keeps a change of ownership and a payout as two separate, visible events rather than one motion.
admin.refusal.coolingTitle: Payouts are paused while the roster settles
admin.refusal.feePolicy.coolingBody: The list of owners changed within the last 48 hours. The owners can be asked again at {at}. The pause is deliberate: it keeps a change of ownership and a change of terms as two separate, visible events rather than one motion.
admin.refusal.feePolicy.coolingBodyNoTim: The list of owners changed within the last 48 hours, and changes of terms stay paused until that period lifts. The pause is deliberate: it keeps a change of ownership and a change of terms as two separate, visible events rather than one motion.
admin.refusal.feePolicy.coolingTitle: Changes of terms are paused while the roster settles
admin.refusal.feePolicy.floorBody: Tightening the terms beyond the house envelope needs more than half of the owners to agree, and with {n, plural, one {# owner} other {# owners}} that bar can never be met. Adding owners restores it; a change within the envelope needs no vote.
admin.refusal.feePolicy.floorBodyNoCount: Tightening the terms beyond the house envelope needs more than half of the owners to agree, and this fund has too few owners for that bar to be met. Adding owners restores it; a change within the envelope needs no vote.
admin.refusal.feePolicy.floorTitle: This fund cannot put a change of terms to its owners
admin.refusal.feePolicy.mailBody: Owners receive their approval link by email, and no mailer is wired — so a proposal opened now could never be voted on and would simply expire. This has to be configured before the owners can be asked about a change of terms.
admin.refusal.floorBody: A payout needs more than half of the owners to agree, and with {n, plural, one {# owner} other {# owners}} that bar can never be met. Adding owners restores it.
admin.refusal.floorBodyNoCount: A payout needs more than half of the owners to agree, and this fund has too few owners for that bar to be met. Adding owners restores it.
admin.refusal.floorTitle: This fund cannot authorise a payout
admin.refusal.mailBody: Owners receive their approval link by email, and no mailer is wired — so a proposal opened now could never be voted on and would simply expire. This has to be configured before the fund can pay itself out.
admin.revenue.bankingTreasuryNote: Withdrawal fees land here, not in the fee allocation: banking's own cash, held by no one through units. Nothing is paid out of it until scope approvals cover treasury spending.
admin.revenue.grant.intro: Seat a person on the fee allocation. The owners are asked; the units are minted only when more than half of them agree.
admin.revenue.grant.opened: The owners have each been emailed a link. No units are minted until more than half of them confirm from their own mailboxes; the cap table above follows once the relay posts the grant.
admin.revenue.ownMoneyNote: This is the platform's own money. Client balances and the fund allocation are separate ledger claims and are not included here — and cannot be reached from this screen.
admin.revenue.subtitle: What the platform earned — the fee allocation: its cash, its units and who holds them
admin.revenue.toPayments: Moving the platform's earnings — into a product, or to an investor — is a payment order the owners authorise. Open one there. Cash reaches the chain only through a holder's redemption and their own withdrawal.
admin.revenue.toTreasury: The fee allocation beside the platform's other balances: custody per rail, user claims, every allocation and its holders.
admin.revenue.unitsHint: units of the fee allocation, held by people
admin.valuation.capBelowIssued: Below the {n} units already issued: this stops further issuance. Nothing minted is affected and redemptions keep working.
admin.valuation.capHint: Takes effect on the next subscription. Redemptions are never affected.
admin.valuation.capInvalid: Must be greater than zero — to stop new money entirely, close the allocation instead.
admin.valuation.derivedFormula: = AUM / {n, plural, one {# unit} other {# units}}
admin.valuation.loadingSupply: Loading supply… — a subscription that would mint past the cap is refused.
admin.valuation.navGuardNote: NAV-move guard — a post is refused if the NAV moves more than 50% from the last mark or from the mark of a week ago, so stepping there in smaller posts is refused too. Nothing overrides it: a larger move is put to the owners' vote instead.
admin.valuation.noUnitsNote: No units outstanding — NAV is {formula}, so it is undefined until someone subscribes. The fund prices at the seed NAV 1.0 until the first subscription; there is nothing to mark yet.
admin.valuation.pickAFund: Pick a fund above to see and resize its authorised unit supply.
admin.valuation.proposeHint: A move past the guard is put to the owners' vote instead of being posted.
admin.valuation.proposedBody: Nothing is marked yet. Every owner has been emailed a link; once more than half of them agree, {service} is marked at {aum} USDT. The live tally is in the consilium.
admin.valuation.queueEmptyHint: A request appears here when an investor asks to redeem units.
admin.valuation.queueFootnote: Settle pays at settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid; if the rail is short the payout queues until treasury tops up. Fail voids the request and refunds the units.
admin.valuation.stillIssuable: {units} units still issuable — a subscription that would mint past the cap is refused.
admin.valuation.subtitle: Post fund NAV and clear the redemption queue

invest.about.risk: Units can fall in value as well as rise. The NAV is set by a posted valuation, not by a market price, and past marks are no guide to future ones. Cash comes back only when a redemption settles or a buyer takes your units on the book. Invest only what you can afford to leave in.
invest.about.title: About this product
invest.backing.inKindNote: Units of this product represent an asset held off-platform. The fund holds no cash for them, so they are sold on the book rather than redeemed.
invest.blocked.capReached: This fund has issued its full authorised supply, so it is not minting new units. Redemptions are unaffected.
invest.blocked.closed: This fund is closed to new subscriptions. Your units are unaffected — you can still redeem them in full.
invest.blocked.locked: This fund isn't open to you yet. You can see it, but subscribing stays locked until your access is raised. If you think you should have it:
invest.blocked.staleNav: The fund's valuation is out of date, so dealing is paused until a fresh one is posted.
invest.buysUnits: Buys {n, plural, one {{units} unit} other {{units} units}} at {nav} USDT per unit.
invest.dustHint: Too small to buy a whole unit at {nav} — increase the amount.
invest.facts.feeHeadlineHurdle: {management} p.a. + {performance} of the gain above {hurdle} p.a.
invest.facts.liquidityNavOrBook: Redeem at NAV (queued) or trade on the book
invest.feeChangeProposed: A change is proposed and awaits the owners: {terms}.
invest.feeNoteHolder: Fees are taken in units, never in cash — your wallet balance is untouched, and the value shown opposite is before them. The performance fee applies only to gains above your own high-water mark, so a recovery back to it costs nothing.
invest.feeNoteProspect: Fees are taken in units, never in cash. The performance fee applies only to gains above the price you enter at, measured per investor rather than per fund.
invest.fullyIssued: Fully issued — not minting new units.
invest.insufficientHint: That is more than your available balance.
invest.noFunds: No funds are open for subscription right now.
invest.noFundsHint: A fund appears here once it is registered and opened for subscription. Nothing you hold is affected.
invest.noUnitsInFund: You hold no units in this fund yet.
invest.notRegisteredHint: Nothing is registered under this name. If you followed a link here, the product may never have been opened.
invest.notYetValuedHint: Not yet valued — the first subscription prices at 1.0.
invest.overCapHint: Only {n, plural, one {{units} unit is} other {{units} units are}} left before this fund reaches its cap — reduce the amount.
invest.redeemEstimate: ≈ {amount} USDT at today's NAV — the settle price may differ.
invest.redeemReceiptCompleted: {n, plural, one {{units} unit} other {{units} units}} redeemed for {cash} USDT at {nav} USDT NAV.
invest.redeemReceiptQueued: {n, plural, one {{units} unit} other {{units} units}} reserved — queued until the fund tops up, then priced at the settle NAV.
invest.redeemTimingNote: Your units are reserved the moment you submit, but the cash is priced when the redemption settles — not now. A figure shown here is an estimate at today's NAV.
invest.redeemUnbacked: Units of this product are not backed by fund cash — sell them on the book instead of redeeming.
invest.subscribeIdleHint: Units are priced at the current NAV; the unit count is fixed at purchase and does not grow.
invest.subscribeReceiptBody: Minted {n, plural, one {{units} unit} other {{units} units}} at {nav} USDT NAV — your position updates shortly.
invest.subscribeVerifyBody: Subscriptions open once your identity is verified. Your balance is untouched in the meantime.
invest.supplyNote: Subscriptions mint units at the current NAV. Once the cap is reached the fund stops accepting new money; redemptions are unaffected.

invest.unmarkedNote: No valuation posted yet — units price at the bootstrap NAV of 1.0 until the first mark.
invest.youHoldUnits: You hold {n, plural, one {{units} unit} other {{units} units}}.

tips.admin.cabinet.announcement.live.bod: Publishes the announcement banner across the whole cabinet immediately.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.body: Flags gate cabinet features and MFE mounts. The row toggle flips a flag on or off; the rollout % controls what share of users it is exposed to.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.rollout.body: The share of users the flag is enabled for during a staged rollout. 100% is a full rollout; lower values expose it to only that fraction.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.rollout.title: Rollout %
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.title: Feature flags
tips.admin.cabinet.maintenance.body: Swaps the whole cabinet for a holding page for all users — an identity-plane kill-switch. No money movement is affected.
tips.admin.cabinet.maintenance.title: Maintenance mode
tips.admin.cabinet.readonly.body: Halts all deposit and withdrawal money movement — the money-plane kill-switch.
tips.admin.cabinet.readonly.title: Read-only mode
tips.admin.outbox.parked-events.body: A row parks when the relay hits a terminal apply error. Fix the cause shown in the Reason column first, then unpark to re-drive it — otherwise it just re-parks.
tips.admin.outbox.parked-events.title: Parked events
tips.admin.outbox.parked.compensated.bod: This row's saga was already reversed, so its money effect is undone. Unpark is disabled to avoid re-applying an entry that was intentionally rolled back.
tips.admin.outbox.parked.reason.body: The relay's failure cause for this parked row — the thing you must fix before unparking.
tips.admin.outbox.parked.reason.title: Reason
tips.admin.outbox.parked.unpark.body: Re-drives this outbox row through the relay after you've fixed its cause. Disabled when the row was compensated, already unparked this session, or while another unpark is in flight.
tips.admin.outbox.parked.unpark.title: Unpark
tips.admin.treasury.bank.body: The fiat USD bank balance used for off-ramp and FX, counted as treasury liquidity alongside the on-chain rails.
tips.admin.treasury.bank.title: Bank · USD
tips.admin.treasury.invariant.body: Per-rail backing is the treasury's job, not the ledger's: a shortfall on one rail is accept-and-queue, then rebalanced via CEX, alt-rail, or top-up. The global invariant is sum(custody) == sum(claims).
tips.admin.treasury.invariant.title: The invariant
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.allocations.b: Every allocation's cash claim, supply, price and holders — the products and the hidden fee and fund allocations. Every unit belongs to a person or to the fee allocation; nothing is nobody's.
Total claims — users' and allocations'. Equals the sum of on-chain custody — every claim is fully backed.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.held-by-users: Claims people hold directly — their wallet balances. Read off the user claim accounts, never derived as a remainder.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.ledger.body: The ledger's network-agnostic claims in USDT. Total claims equal on-chain custody and break down into what users hold directly, what allocations hold for their holders, and reserved-for-withdrawals.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.ledger.title: Layer 1 · Ledger
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.reserved-with: Claims set aside for queued and in-flight withdrawals, parked in the clearing account until they settle on-chain.
tips.admin.treasury.layer2.rails.body: The actual on-chain USDT liquidity held per rail (BEP20 / TRC20 / TON / Polygon), plus the fiat bank balance. This is where the backing physically sits.
tips.admin.treasury.layer2.rails.title: Layer 2 · Treasury
tips.admin.treasury.rail.address.body: This rail's on-chain hot-wallet address. BEP20 and Polygon share an identical EVM address format — topping up on the wrong EVM chain, or sending another rail's funds here, is an irreversible mis-send.
tips.admin.treasury.rail.address.title: Treasury address
tips.admin.treasury.rail.funding.body: The card value is this rail's ledger custody; the footer shows the hot wallet's real on-chain USDT and native gas. The two can legitimately diverge under accept-and-queue.
tips.admin.treasury.rail.funding.title: Rail funding
tips.admin.treasury.rail.gas-station.bod: Top this address up with the rail's native token to fund sweep gas. Send the correct native symbol on the correct chain — EVM gas-station addresses are shared, so a wrong-chain top-up is unrecoverable.
tips.admin.treasury.two-layer-model.body: Layer 1 is the ledger's network-agnostic USDT claims; Layer 2 is the actual on-chain liquidity held per rail. The two must reconcile.
tips.admin.users.access.kyc-level.body: The user's identity-verification tier. Higher levels unlock higher limits and actions per the KYC policy.
tips.admin.users.access.kyc-level.title: KYC level
Bumps token_version — invalidates every JWT issued to this user, signing them out of every active session.
tips.admin.users.access.role.body: The access level for this user: investor, operator or admin. Raising it grants operator/admin console access immediately on change. Owner is not here — a seat is the consilium's to give and to take away.
tips.admin.users.access.role.title: Role
A per-user counter stamped into every issued JWT. It increments on 'Revoke all sessions', so any token carrying an older version fails verification.
tips.admin.users.status.suspend.body: Hold freezes the account now and lapses by itself in 24 hours — one operator may do that. Making it permanent, or undoing a permanent one, is a proposal the owners vote through. An account blocked before the two were told apart does not lapse, and one admin can lift it.
tips.admin.users.status.suspend.title: Hold, suspension and reinstatement
tips.admin.valuation.post.aum.body: The fund's total assets under management you're marking. The NAV/share that pays redemptions is derived from it (AUM ÷ units outstanding), so a wrong figure mis-prices every settle.
tips.admin.valuation.post.aum.title: AUM (USDT)
tips.admin.valuation.post.derived-nav.bo: Entered AUM divided by units outstanding. This is the mark that Post valuation commits.
tips.admin.valuation.post.nav-guard.body: A post is refused if the NAV moves more than 50% from the last mark or from the mark of a week ago — stepping there in smaller posts is refused too. There is no override: a larger move is proposed to the owners and recorded only if their vote carries.
tips.admin.valuation.post.propose.body: Opens a consilium instead of posting. The owners answer from their mailboxes; if more than half agree, the fund is marked at this AUM regardless of the NAV-move guard. Nothing changes until then.
tips.admin.valuation.post.propose.title: Propose to the owners
tips.admin.valuation.queue.est-cash.body: A preview only — approximately units × current NAV. The actual payout settles at the settle-time NAV, not this figure.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.fail.body: Voids the request and refunds the units — no cash is paid and the burned units are returned to the user.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.fail.title: Fail
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle-fail.b: Settle pays at settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid; if the rail is short the payout queues until treasury tops up. Fail voids the request and refunds the units.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle.body: Pays at the settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid, queuing if the rail is short. Settle also burns the user's units.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle.title: Settle
tips.admin.withdrawals.destination.body: The user's payout address, bound to this specific rail. Sends are irreversible and rail-specific — verify the address matches the network before dispatching.
tips.admin.withdrawals.destination.title: Destination
tips.admin.withdrawals.fail.double-pay.b: Failing refunds the user. If the broadcast reached the chain this would double-pay — the hub refuses while a broadcast record exists, but verify on-chain first.
tips.admin.withdrawals.flow.body: Dispatch broadcasts a queued withdrawal once its rail has liquidity. Settle records the mined transaction and releases the reservation. Fail voids and refunds — only safe when nothing reached the chain.
tips.admin.withdrawals.flow.title: Dispatch, settle, fail
tips.admin.withdrawals.gross-net.body: Gross is the full amount debited from the user; net is what is actually sent on-chain after the withdrawal fee.
tips.admin.withdrawals.gross-net.title: Gross / net
tips.admin.withdrawals.settle.tx-hash.bo: Paste the mined on-chain tx hash. Settling records the mined transaction and releases the reservation — only enter a hash for a tx that actually mined.
tips.admin.withdrawals.state.body: Queued = accepted and reserved but not yet broadcast (Dispatch only). Processing = already broadcast, awaiting a mined tx (Settle or Fail apply).
tips.admin.withdrawals.state.title: State
tips.dashboard.invested.allocation.body: Each bar is one strategy's share of your invested value at current NAV. Percentages are of invested value only and exclude your available cash.
tips.dashboard.invested.allocation.title: Invested — what I own
tips.dashboard.performance.all-time-retu: Total unrealized P&L divided by what you put in at cost basis, across every position. A paper figure, not realized cash.
tips.dashboard.performance.portfolio-val: Your whole balance: available + invested + pending withdrawal. Money locked in a queued withdrawal is still counted here.
tips.dashboard.performance.series.body: 'Fund performance' is the fund's return since the first valuation in the range, from the posted marks; 'Your participation' is what your units were worth at each of them, which differs by when you contributed.
tips.dashboard.performance.series.title: Performance chart
tips.dashboard.stats.available.body: Cash that is free and spendable now — ready to deploy into a strategy or withdraw.
tips.dashboard.stats.available.title: Available
tips.dashboard.stats.net-invested.body: Total cash you put into strategies at cost basis, net of redemptions — not the current value.
tips.dashboard.stats.net-invested.title: Net invested
tips.dashboard.stats.unrealized-pnl.body: Paper gain or loss across all positions — current value minus cost basis. It becomes realized cash only when you redeem.
tips.invest.activity.cancel.body: Available only while a redemption is still queued. It withdraws the request and releases the reserved units back to your holding before any settle NAV is applied.
tips.invest.activity.cancel.title: Cancel
tips.invest.activity.status.body: Queued (reserved, awaiting settle), completed (paid out at the settle NAV), failed, or cancelled.
tips.invest.activity.status.title: Redemption status
tips.invest.overview.body: Subscribe USDT for units — your value tracks the fund's NAV, not the unit count.
tips.invest.overview.title: How investing works
tips.invest.position.nav.body: Net asset value per unit — the current price at which units are bought on subscribe and priced on redeem.
tips.invest.position.nav.title: NAV
tips.invest.position.pnl.body: Your position's current value minus what you paid in — green for a gain, red for a loss, driven by the NAV moving.
tips.invest.position.pnl.title: Profit & loss
tips.invest.position.stale-nav.body: The fund's price feed is out of date, so the value and P&L shown here may lag the true mark until the NAV refreshes.
tips.invest.position.stale-nav.title: Stale NAV
tips.invest.position.units.body: The units you hold in this fund — a fixed quantity until you subscribe or redeem more.
tips.invest.position.units.title: Units
tips.invest.position.value.body: Units × current NAV. It rises and falls as the NAV moves, not with the unit count.
tips.invest.position.value.title: Value
tips.invest.redeem.queue.body: Redemptions are accept-and-queue — your units are reserved now, and cash is priced at the settle-time NAV once the fund tops up.
tips.invest.redeem.queue.title: How redemptions settle
tips.invest.redeem.units.body: How many units to redeem — Max fills your full holding. The resulting cash isn't fixed here; it is set at the settle-time NAV.
tips.invest.redeem.units.title: Units to redeem
tips.invest.subscribe.amount.body: How much USDT to subscribe. It is converted into units at the current NAV when you submit.
tips.invest.subscribe.amount.title: Amount
tips.profile.email.verified.body: Confirms this email address has been verified. It is not identity or KYC verification.
tips.profile.email.verified.title: Verified
tips.profile.field.legal-name.body: Your full name exactly as it appears on official documents — used for compliance and statements, distinct from your preferred name.
tips.profile.field.legal-name.title: Legal name
tips.profile.field.nationality.body: Collected for compliance and eligibility checks.
tips.profile.field.nationality.title: Nationality
tips.profile.field.tax-residence.body: The country where you're liable to pay tax, used for tax reporting. Usually where you live — it can differ from your nationality.
tips.profile.field.tax-residence.title: Tax residence
tips.profile.kyc-level.body: Level 0 is browse only: products, prices and your account. Level 1 means your identity is verified and opens a deposit address, withdrawals and subscribing.
tips.profile.kyc-level.title: What your KYC level means
tips.profile.personal.compliance.body: These personal details are collected to meet the fund's compliance obligations and to produce your account statements. They are not shown publicly.
tips.profile.personal.compliance.title: Why we collect this
tips.settings.security.google-signin.bod: Your sign-in and password are managed by Google. Two-factor authentication and recovery are configured in your Google Account.
tips.settings.sessions.overview.body: Where you're signed in — each row is a device or browser with a live session. Revoke anything you don't recognise.
tips.settings.sessions.overview.title: Sessions & devices
tips.settings.sessions.revoke-others.bod: Signs out every device except this one. Use it if a device was lost or you don't recognise a session.
tips.settings.sessions.revoke.body: Signs that device out immediately. It must sign in again with Google to regain access.
tips.settings.sessions.revoke.title: Revoke
tips.settings.sessions.this-device.body: The browser you're using right now. It stays signed in and can't be revoked from here — use 'Sign out all other devices' to clear the rest.
tips.settings.sessions.this-device.title: This device
tips.trade.book.body: The book trades existing units between holders — a buyer and a seller meet at a bid or ask price they set themselves. Subscribing is different: it mints new units at the posted NAV, and redeeming returns them at NAV.
tips.trade.book.title: How the book works
tips.wallet.balance.available.body: Your spendable USDT right now — what you can invest into fund units or withdraw.
tips.wallet.balance.available.title: Available
tips.wallet.balance.in-compartments.body: USDT you moved into a service's compartment. Still yours and counted in your total — move it back to your main balance to withdraw it.
tips.wallet.balance.in-orders.body: USDT set aside by your resting buy orders on the book. Still yours: it comes back to available when an order is cancelled, and turns into units when it fills.
tips.wallet.balance.in-orders.title: In orders
tips.wallet.balance.invested.body: Held in fund units, valued at the current NAV — units offered for sale on the book included.
tips.wallet.balance.invested.title: Invested
tips.wallet.balance.model.body: You have a single USDT balance — networks are just how you deposit and withdraw. This card splits it into Total = Available + In orders + Invested + Pending withdrawal + In compartments.
tips.wallet.balance.model.title: One balance, many networks
tips.wallet.balance.pending-withdrawal.b: USDT reserved for withdrawals still in flight (queued or processing). It is no longer part of your available balance.
tips.wallet.deposit.address.body: A personal, reusable address on this network. On TON it is shown in the wallet-friendly UQ… form so an uninitialised wallet doesn't bounce the transfer.
tips.wallet.deposit.address.title: Your deposit address
tips.wallet.deposit.min-confirmations.bo: Credited to your one balance after the required number of network confirmations.
tips.wallet.deposit.network.body: Pick the chain you'll send USDT on. Each network shows its own deposit address below — that address only works on that one chain.
tips.wallet.deposit.network.title: Network
tips.wallet.deposit.rail-hazard.body: Sending any other asset, or using a different network, loses the funds permanently. This 0x address is NOT your address on the sibling EVM chain — even though both start with 0x, USDT sent on the wrong EVM network will not be credited.
tips.wallet.deposit.rail-hazard.title: Send only USDT on this network
tips.wallet.withdraw.available.body: The most you can withdraw on this network right now. Tap Max to fill the amount.
tips.wallet.withdraw.available.title: Available to withdraw
tips.wallet.withdraw.destination.body: The on-chain address the USDT is sent to. Withdrawals are irreversible — make sure it is correct and on the network you selected.
tips.wallet.withdraw.destination.title: Destination address
tips.wallet.withdraw.network-fee.body: A flat on-chain fee for this network, deducted from your amount before it is sent.
tips.wallet.withdraw.network-fee.title: Network fee
tips.wallet.withdraw.network.body: The chain your withdrawal ships on. The destination address must be a valid address on this exact network, or the funds are lost.
tips.wallet.withdraw.network.title: Network
tips.wallet.withdraw.queueing.body: Up to your instant limit pays out immediately on this network; anything above it is queued until the network is topped up. A minimum applies per withdrawal.
tips.wallet.withdraw.queueing.title: How withdrawals work
tips.wallet.withdraw.review.body: Review freezes exactly what you'll send. Confirm submits that snapshot — if the network list changes underneath, the open review is voided and you re-review.
tips.wallet.withdraw.review.title: Review, then confirm
tips.wallet.withdraw.you-receive.body: Your amount minus the network fee — this is what actually lands at the destination.
tips.wallet.withdraw.you-receive.title: You will receive
trade.book.emptyHint: No holder has quoted yet. The first limit order opens the book.
trade.book.title: Book
trade.chart.empty: No trades yet — the chart draws from the first fill.
trade.chart.title: Chart
trade.form.closed: The book is closed. Orders are not accepted until it opens again.
trade.form.locked: Trading isn't open to you on this product. If you think you should have access:
trade.form.placed.cancelled: Nothing crossed, so the order was cancelled.
trade.form.placed.filled: Filled {filled} at an average of {avg} USDT.
trade.form.placed.partial: Filled {filled} of {size} at {avg} USDT; the rest was cancelled.
trade.form.placed.resting: Resting on the book: {filled} of {size} filled so far.
trade.form.problem.lot: Size must be a multiple of {lot}
trade.form.problem.noQuote: Nothing on the other side to trade against — place a limit order instead.
trade.form.problem.tick: Price must be a multiple of {tick}
trade.form.refusedBody: {detail} If you think you should be able to trade this product:
trade.form.tifHint.alo: Only rests on the book: it is refused rather than filled against an existing order.
trade.form.tifHint.gtc: Rests on the book until it fills or you cancel it.
trade.form.tifHint.ioc: Fills whatever it can right now; the rest is cancelled at once.
trade.ticker.navHint: The book price is what holders trade at; NAV is the fund's own mark.
trade.unbackedNotice: Units of this product are a claim on an off-platform asset and cannot be redeemed for fund cash — the book is the only exit.
wallet.subtitle: Your invest balance and the main account behind it
wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.unavailable: The wallet could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
